headline: Bruins’ Nikita Zadorov fined for roughing Blackhawks’ Alex Vlasic
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Bruins defenseman Nikita Zadorov was fined for roughing Blackhawks defenseman Alex Vlasic, after Boston beat Chicago 5-4 in overtime on Saturday. As The Athletic's Scott Powers posted, "Vlasic and Mittelstadt get two minutes for roughing. Zadorov gets a 10-minute misconduct."

The fine matters less than what the two teams' numbers show. Boston is 10-4-1, but the record flatters them a little: they've drawn about even in chance quality, with a 50.5 percent share of expected goals (a measure of how good the shots each side gets). Goalies have done the lifting, saving 11.5 goals more than expected so far this season. Chicago, 4-9-1, has been outplayed (43.2 percent) and is 8 goals short of what its chances should have produced, so some of that record is bad finishing luck. As for the two defensemen, both are pointless in goals through 14 games, and both have been slightly worse for their teams with them on the ice, by about two and a half points of expected goal share. Vlasic's 39 percent at five-on-five is the bigger concern, and he plays 20.5 minutes a night.
